fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. Paul says the son by the slave woman "…was born according to the flesh…" (Galatians 4:23). That son was Ishmael, Hagar's boy (Genesis 16:15), born after Sarai gave Hagar to her husband Abram as a wife (Genesis 16:3). That's the birth Paul calls "flesh." His brother Isaac was different, because God had told Abraham that Sarah would bear him a son (Genesis 17:19).

Right on, baker. The son by the free woman "…was born through the promise." (Galatians 4:23). That son was Isaac, and God had said ahead of time that Sarah would bear Abraham a son (Genesis 17:19). The other son, Ishmael, is the one Paul says was born according to the flesh. His birth came after Sarai gave Hagar to Abram as a wife (Genesis 16:3).

problems.problem: It explains the promise but does not explain what being born according to the flesh means.
